title: Softwood lumber: nominal name to minimum dressed dry size, with the lengths it is racked in

citation.standard: Voluntary Product Standard PS 20-25, American Softwood Lumber Standard (January 2025)
citation.publisher: U.S. Department of Commerce / National Institute of Standards and Technology, for the American Lumber Standard Committee
citation.where: Table 3, "Nominal and minimum-dressed sizes of boards, dimension, and timbers", page 15 — the Dry columns (thicknesses and widths), which are the sizes of lumber at 19 percent or less moisture content (§2.7, §6.2.3). The Green columns of the same table are deliberately not carried: a green 2x4 is 1-9/16 in x 3-9/16 in. PS 20-25 states that the imperial values are the units of record and the metric ones are given for information only. EDITIONS: these rows were also checked against the previous edition, PS 20-20 (January 2020), whose Table 3 gives identical inch values in every cell carried here; only the metric conversions gained a decimal place.

standardLengthCitation.standard: Standard No. 17, Grading Rules for West Coast Lumber, 2018 Standard Grading Rules (approved by the ALSC Board of Review)
standardLengthCitation.where: ¶2-i ("Standard lengths are multiples of 1' but are customarily shipped in multiples of 2' in most items") and ¶260-a, Table of Random Lengths, All West Coast Species, items (f) Boards, (h) Structural Framing and (i) Beams and Stringers, Posts and Timbers.

entries.name: 1x2
entries.derivation: Table 3, Boards. Thicknesses: nominal 1 in -> 19 mm (3/4 in) dry. Widths: nominal 2 in -> 38 mm (1-1/2 in) dry.
entries.standardLengthDerivation: ¶260-a(f), BOARDS in Select Merchantable, Construction and Standard grades: 6' to 16' or longer. ¶2-i gives the customary 2 ft step, so 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 ft. Longer lengths may be included at the shipper's option, so this is what a yard reliably racks and not a maximum.

entries.standardLengthDerivation: ¶260-a(f), BOARDS: 6' to 16' or longer, stepped by 2 ft per ¶2-i.

entries.name: 6x6
entries.derivation: Table 3, Timbers, which states an amount taken off the nominal size rather than a finished cell. Thicknesses, 5 & 6 thick: 13 mm (1/2 in) off dry, so 6 - 1/2 = 5-1/2 in. Widths, 5 & 6 wide: 1/2 in off, so 6 - 1/2 = 5-1/2 in.
